title: Investigation signal sculpting & experiment feedback loop - notes
content:
Purpose: capture pragmatic heuristics for shaping observability signals (metrics + traces) that support fast investigation during experiments and feature rollouts, while staying within query and storage budgets. This is intended as a lightweight working playbook — focused on what to change in dashboards, sampling, and metric shapes in the first 24h, 7d, and 30d after an experiment launch.

Context / motivation:
- We run a lot of small-to-medium experiments (model variants, routing policies, KV-cache policies, batching knobs). Investigations are time-sensitive: product teams need a clear path from symptom -> hypothesis -> signal refinement -> rollback/rollforward.
- Observability must be both informative (high signal-to-noise) and cost-conscious (query budgets, trace retention). Too many raw time series + full tracing on high-traffic routes floods the SRE/eng queue.
- This doc sits between the instrumentation playbooks and dashboards: it tells engineers how to "sculpt" signals for an experiment and how to feed evidence back to metric owners.

Quick glossary (used in the heuristics below):
- Sculpting: reducing dimensions and adding aggregate anchors so that a single dashboard tile tells a clear investigative story.
- Anchor metric: a low-cardinality, high-level metric that quickly indicates health (e.g., p95 latency for route X, token cost per request).
- Probe metric: a focused diagnostic metric with slightly higher cardinality used for drilldowns (e.g., batch size distribution for model Y).
- Trace-anchor: a sampling strategy or trace tag combination used to capture representative traces for the current hypothesis.

24h playbook (first-response, immediate actions)
- Create a 1-row experiment summary at top of the team's investigation dashboard: experiment id, change description, start time, owner, contact slack. Keep it manual but visible.
- Add or ensure these anchor metrics are present and pinned:
  - request_count (per-minute, route-level)
  - p95_latency_ms (route + model family)
  - error_rate (5xx + client_error_4xx)
  - tokens_per_request (mean)
  - cost_estimate_per_minute (derived, coarse)
- Reduce series cardinality for these anchors: for 24h use grouping = route, model_family, region. Drop tenant-level split unless it's the experiment tenant.
- Tracing: enable focused trace sampling on new or impacted routes only. Strategy: 1% global + 100% for requests matching experiment_id OR route=experiment-route and latency>p90. Add trace-tag experiment_id.
- Quick diagnostic tiles to add:
  - batch_size_histogram (last 2h, stream) — bucketed at [1,2,4,8,16,>16]
  - kv_cache_hit_rate (per route, last 2h)
  - inflight_requests (per pod/shard)
- Run a 30-minute synthetic probe hitting the experiment route at steady QPS to sanity-check golden metrics. Pin the probe run in the doc.

7d playbook (short-term investigation and stabilization)
- If anomalies persist beyond 24h: expand anchor dimensions to include customer_tier and instance_type (to catch skew).
- Create probe metric dashboards: a single page with 6 tiles that map to the top hypotheses (e.g., batching misalignment, cold KV cache, routing misconfiguration, quantization boundary issues). Each tile must include: metric definition, owner, and a recommended drilldown query.
- Tracing: refine adaptive sampling budget by adding severity weighting: traces that show latency>500ms or errors get 5x higher sample weight. Update SLO for trace budget to avoid overruns.
- Alerting: convert any ad-hoc p95 guardrails into temporary alerts with a 10m throttle and a low-noise notification routing (pager vs slack) depending on experiment severity.
- Cost pruning: enable retention-tiering for experiment traces (7d full, 30d summary) and downsample metric granularity from 1m to 5m after 48h if no regressions.

30d playbook (postmortem & telemetry hygiene)
- Decide which signals to keep as long-term: keep anchor metrics, keep 1-2 probe metrics if they consistently helped root cause. Archive or delete the rest.
- Convert useful ad-hoc probes into instrumentation tasks (Jira) with metric owners assigned.
- Trace retention: keep full traces for repro vs keep aggregated flamegraphs for longer-term model-ops analysis.
- Add a short note to the experiment's rollup: how observability changes affected investigation time and cost (simple delta on trace volume and query costs).

Metric definition mini-spec (how to write metrics so they're probe-friendly)
- Name: lower_snake_case, include scope postfix (e.g., "_route", "_model_family"). Examples: request_count_route, p95_latency_ms_route, kv_cache_hit_rate_model_family.
- Type: counter | gauge | histogram (explicit)
- Aggregation: default to count/sum on ingestion, expose p50/p90/p95 histograms if latency/hist.
- Cardinality guidance: list allowed labels and recommended cardinality caps. Example: request_count_route labels = [route, model_family, region] (<=200 unique combos in prod dashboard).
- Provenance: include a short provenance tag on metric (instrumentation PR link or owning-service).

Trace-sampling design notes (practical)
- Tag experiments early in the request path (experiment_id, feature_flag, rollout_bucket) so sampling rules can pick them.
- Maintain a per-experiment trace-budget annotation. Example: "budget: 10k traces/day for EXP-1234". Use it to dynamically lower sample rate of other services if budget nears exhaustion.
- Prefer severity-weighted sampling (latency+error+resource-saturation) over pure random. This preserves rarer failures.

Dashboard pruning & composition heuristics
- Keep each page to <= 8 tiles for rapid scanning. If more diagnostics are needed, create a "deep-dive" page linked from the top.
- Tile pattern: anchor -> probe -> trace-anchor -> owner/action. That order helps a responder go from overview to evidence to next action.
- Use visual annotations: experiment start/stop overlays, probe run markers, and release flags. Visuals reduce cognitive load during war-room sessions.
- Query budget guardrail: every new dashboard should include an estimate of daily query cost (rough calc based on sample rate and retention). Put that estimate in the page header.

Investigation workflow (play-by-play) - recommended checklist for whoever owns the experiment:
1) Reproduce: run the synthetic probe and confirm anchor deviations.
2) Hypothesize: pick top 1-2 hypotheses and map them to probe metrics.
3) Sculpt: add probe tiles with reduced cardinality and set trace-anchor rules.
4) Collect: run with increased trace sampling for 2h or until you have 50-200 representative traces.
5) Analyze: tag suspects, create a short summary and next-action (rollback/patch/tweak config).
6) Communicate: post short findings to #prod-experiments and tag product/owner.
7) Close: update experiment doc with telemetry delta and file instrumentation tickets for long-term signals.

Practical gotchas / notes to self:
- If a probe metric suddenly shows a lot of new labels, add a collapse rule (e.g., map unknown labels to "other") to avoid dashboard explosion.
- Don’t blindly turn on full tracing for a high-QPS route — blooms costs quickly. Use anchor-based triggers (latency > threshold) to escalate sampling.
- Beware of cost drift: small increases in trace retention or histogram buckets can double storage over months. Add changes to monthly telemetry budget review.

Open questions (for TA/owners):
- How should we auto-provision experiment dashboards on feature flag creation? (manual vs templated vs infra-auto)
- Can we create a central small UX widget that always shows experiment budget remaining (traces + queries)?

Action items (next steps):
- [Avery] Draft experiment dashboard template and post to Confluence (target: 2026-02-12).
- [Marcus] Prototype severity-weighted sampling rules in staging (target: 2026-02-26).
- [Sofia] Add a small query-cost estimator to dashboard headers (spike, target: 2w).

Appendix: quick example metric declarations (copy/paste friendly)
- request_count_route: type=counter; labels=[route,model_family,region]; agg=count
- p95_latency_ms_route: type=histogram; labels=[route,model_family]; buckets=exp(2..2048ms)
- kv_cache_hit_rate_model_family: type=gauge; labels=[model_family]; agg=ratio(cache_hits, cache_lookups)

End of doc.
